sn40.10:1.1.pli: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva—jetavane antarahito devesu tāvatiṃsesu pāturahosi.
sn40.10:1.1.eng: And then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared among the gods of the thirty-three.
sn40.10:1.1.comm: As at SN 55.18 and SN 55.19; see too MN 37:15.

sn40.10:1.2.pli: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca:
sn40.10:1.2.eng: Then Sakka, lord of gods, with five hundred deities came up to Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, and stood to one side. Mahāmoggallāna said to him:

sn40.10:2.1.eng: “Lord of gods, it’s good to go for refuge to the Buddha.

sn40.10:2.2.pli: Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.
sn40.10:2.2.eng: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn40.10:2.3.eng: It’s good to go for refuge to the teaching.

sn40.10:2.4.pli: Dhammasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.
sn40.10:2.4.eng: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn40.10:2.5.eng: It’s good to go for refuge to the Saṅgha.

sn40.10:2.6.pli: Saṅghasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.
sn40.10:2.6.eng: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

sn40.10:7.1.pli: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca:
sn40.10:7.1.eng: Then Sakka, lord of gods, with five hundred deities came up to Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, and stood to one side. Mahāmoggallāna said to him:

sn40.10:8.1.pli: “Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti:
sn40.10:8.1.eng: “Lord of gods, it’s good to have experiential confidence in the Buddha:

sn40.10:8.2.pli: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti.
sn40.10:8.2.eng: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn40.10:8.3.pli: Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.
sn40.10:8.3.eng: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn40.10:9.1.pli: Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti:
sn40.10:9.1.eng: It’s good to have experiential confidence in the teaching:

sn40.10:9.2.pli: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
sn40.10:9.2.eng: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

sn40.10:9.3.pli: Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.
sn40.10:9.3.eng: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn40.10:10.1.pli: Sādhu kho, devānaminda, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti:
sn40.10:10.1.eng: It’s good to have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

sn40.10:10.2.pli: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti.
sn40.10:10.2.eng: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with joined palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

sn40.10:10.3.pli: Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.
sn40.10:10.3.eng: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn40.10:11.1.pli: Sādhu kho, devānaminda, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṃvattanikehi.
sn40.10:11.1.eng: It’s good to have the ethical conduct that’s loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

sn40.10:11.2.pli: Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.
sn40.10:11.2.eng: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.”

sn40.10:37.1.pli: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcahi devatāsatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca:
sn40.10:37.1.eng: Then Sakka, lord of gods, with five hundred deities came up to Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, and stood to one side. Mahāmoggallāna said to him:

sn40.10:38.1.pli: “Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti:
sn40.10:38.1.eng: “Lord of gods, it’s good to have experiential confidence in the Buddha:

sn40.10:38.2.pli: ‘itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti.
sn40.10:38.2.eng: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha … teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

sn40.10:38.3.pli: Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.
sn40.10:38.3.eng: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

sn40.10:38.4.pli: Te aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhanti—
sn40.10:38.4.eng: They surpass other gods in ten respects:

sn40.10:38.5.eng: heavenly lifespan, beauty, happiness, glory, sovereignty, sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches.

sn40.11:7.7.eng: The Linked Discourses on Moggallāna are complete.

sn40.2:0.3.eng: A Question About the Second Absorption

sn40.2:1.1.eng: “They speak of this thing called the ‘second absorption’.

sn40.2:1.4.pli: ‘idha bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.
sn40.2:1.4.eng: ‘As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

sn40.2:1.5.eng: This is called the second absorption.’

sn40.2:1.6.pli: So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi.
sn40.2:1.6.eng: And so … I was entering and remaining in the second absorption.

sn40.2:1.7.pli: Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato vitakkasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.
sn40.2:1.7.eng: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by placing the mind beset me.

sn40.2:2.1.pli: Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca:
sn40.2:2.1.eng: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.2:2.3.pli: Mā, brāhmaṇa, dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ pamādo, dutiye jhāne cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, dutiye jhāne cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, dutiye jhāne cittaṃ samādahā’ti.
sn40.2:2.3.eng: Don’t neglect the second absorption, brahmin! Settle your mind in the second absorption; unify your mind and immerse it in the second absorption.’

sn40.2:2.4.pli: So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ.
sn40.2:2.4.eng: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the second absorption.

sn40.2:2.5.pli: Yañhi taṃ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
sn40.2:2.5.eng: So if anyone should be rightly called

sn40.2:2.6.pli: ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṃ patto’ti, mamaṃ taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
sn40.2:2.6.eng: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

sn40.3:0.3.eng: A Question About the Third Absorption

sn40.3:1.1.eng: “They speak of this thing called the ‘third absorption’.

sn40.3:1.4.pli: idha bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.
sn40.3:1.4.eng: ‘With the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, personally experiencing the bliss of which the noble ones declare, “Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.”

sn40.3:1.5.eng: This is called the third absorption.’

sn40.3:1.6.pli: So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharāmi sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedemi. Yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharāmi.
sn40.3:1.6.eng: And so … I was entering and remaining in the third absorption.

sn40.3:1.7.pli: Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato pītisahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.
sn40.3:1.7.eng: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by rapture beset me.

sn40.3:2.1.pli: Atha kho maṃ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca:
sn40.3:2.1.eng: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

sn40.3:2.3.pli: Mā, brāhmaṇa, tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ pamādo, tatiye jhāne cittaṃ saṇṭhapehi, tatiye jhāne cittaṃ ekodiṃ karohi, tatiye jhāne cittaṃ samādahā’ti.
sn40.3:2.3.eng: Don’t neglect the third absorption, brahmin! Settle your mind in the third absorption; unify your mind and immerse it in the third absorption.’

sn40.3:2.4.pli: So khvāhaṃ, āvuso, aparena samayena pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharāmi sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedemi, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ.
sn40.3:2.4.eng: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the third absorption.

sn40.3:2.5.pli: Yañhi taṃ āvuso sammā vadamāno vadeyya …pe… mahābhiññataṃ patto”ti.
sn40.3:2.5.eng: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”
